attachesAs: a hook written above and to the right of the consonant
compositionOrder: write the Tamil consonant carrier first
write the i sign after it, as a symbol of its own at the right

compositionSource.citation: HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0 User Manual, sections 4 and 4-3 and Table 3: vowel signs that occur as distinct characters to the left or right of the base consonant are recognizer symbols of their own, and syllabic units are written from left to right
compositionSource.variation: Table 3 lists U+0BBE, U+0BBF, U+0BC0, U+0BC6, U+0BC7 and U+0BC8 as symbols of their own, and HP Labs India's notes on the hpl-tamil-iso-char dataset add that these signs leave Tamil 'written linearly as a sequence of visually discrete symbols'. So a sign placed left of its consonant is written before it, and a sign placed right of it is written after it. The manual gives no path for the consonant and no order for a sign fused with its consonant, such as u or the ligature ti.

components: a hook curling to the left
a stem down to the line
strokeOrder: start at the tip of the hook and curl up to the left
without lifting, arch over the top to the right
without lifting, draw the stem down to the line — and only now lift
strokeOrderNote: one continuous stroke — three joined movements, no pen lift; cited to native writers' pen traces in HP Labs India's LipiTk Tamil recognizer, class 37

strokeOrderSource.citation: HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Tamil recognizer, class 37 (ி, i sign): stored online-handwriting prototypes from native Tamil writers (MIT licence, 2012)
strokeOrderSource.variation: The recognizer stores native Tamil writers' tablet pen traces, each resampled to 60 points. 205 of the 206 stored prototypes of the i sign are one pen-down stroke. In 161 of those 205 the pen starts at the tip of the hook and first moves up; 200 turn clockwise, over the top to the right; 152 end at the foot of the stem. The traces are scaled to a square, so they fix the start, the direction and the pen lifts, not the proportions: the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Tamil outline of the sign on its own. Handwriting varies by writer.
